messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital stay: The patient was admitted to the hospital due to the presence of a brain tumor located in the clivus region. He underwent surgical intervention via a left suboccipital craniotomy, which involved resection of the tumor. Oral intubation was done using the Macintosh laryngoscope blade, and the patient was placed in the left park bench position with neck flexion. Surgery was performed via the left lateral suboccipital approach. The lesion was decompressed, and the operation was completed successfully.

Medical Condition at Discharge: The patient had minor swelling in the neck, tongue, and pharynx on the left side. He experienced pain in the tip of his tongue with a small ulcer on the left side after returning to the intensive care unit. The swelling of his tongue gradually improved after the administration of steroids. The patient was discharged 10 days after the surgery.

Follow-Up Care: The patient was advised to undergo follow-up MRI after three months of surgery as well as clinical follow-up as per physician's recommendations.

Discharge Medications: None.

Instructions: The patient was advised to follow-up with his physician for regular check-up and take rest until complete recovery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The admission was for a brain tumor in the clivus region, treated by resection. The histology is not given, so the type of neoplasm is uncertain. Clival tumors are most often chordoma or meningioma. Chordoma codes to C41.0 (malignant neoplasm of bones of skull and face) and meningioma to D32.0 (benign neoplasm of cerebral meninges).

This looks like a published case report about macroglossia or tongue swelling after a suboccipital approach for a clival tumor, so the tumor type could be either. With no histology, a neoplasm of uncertain behaviour is possible (D43.-, or D48.0 for bone). The summary calls it a "brain tumor", so the unspecified-behaviour brain code D43.2 is a candidate. A clival chordoma would be C41.0 in ICD-10.

The principal diagnosis is the reason for admission, which is the tumor. Without histology, I'll go with D43 (neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behaviour of brain and central nervous system).

**D43**
